title: Oil, propane or electric heat, plus AC? A national model says 95 to 100 percent of homes save.

sentences.text: 95 to 100 percent of homes heating with oil, propane or electricity, and already running air conditioning, would pay less with a heat pump, a national study estimates.

assertions.text: For homes heating primarily with electricity, fuel oil or propane and with central or room AC, the study found 95% to 100% nationally would have positive bill savings, depending on heat pump efficiency.
qualifications: s03 says the figure is a modelled estimate of bills, not measured bills; s05 gives the weaker result for the same fuels without air conditioning; the sentence itself limits it to homes that already have AC.

sentences.note: Copied from parent s07.a with the passage's own population: 'electricity', not 'electric baseboards' (the passage covers every home heating primarily with electricity).

sentences.text: Estimates, because it is a model: the study simulated those homes' bills, so the figure is not a reading from anyone's meter.

assertions.text: The study modelled the national stock of homes that heat primarily with electricity, fuel oil or propane and have central or window/room AC, estimating their bill savings rather than measuring them.
qualifications: s03 itself says the result is modelled, not measured.

sentences.note: The modelled nature comes from the study's method (sample homes per PUMA, L385-L388) and the parent's accepted reading of s07 ("estimated", "would see"); the passage's home count is left out so no figure is read that the validator cannot match.

sentences.text: Its median saving, $300 to $650 a year, is for those same homes and moves with the heat pump's efficiency.

assertions.text: For those homes the median bill saving was $300 to $650 per year, depending on efficiency.
qualifications: s04 itself says the median is for those same homes (the fuels and AC named in s01) and moves with the heat pump's efficiency; s03 says it is modelled.

sentences.text: Drop the air conditioning and the same model is weaker: only 73 to 86 percent come out ahead.

assertions.text: Only 73% to 86% of the homes heating with those fuels but without central or room AC would have positive bill savings.
qualifications: s05 itself limits the figure to homes on those fuels without AC; s03 says it is modelled.

sentences.note: Copied from parent s09.a. The parent's s09.b (why those homes lose: new cooling in hot climates) rests on a claim outside this Short's package and is not asserted here.

sentences.text: Whether metered homes agree with the model is the subject of the full inquiry.
